case: T03-v2 control - Slide Scout, read-only browser for local OME-Zarr 0.5 filesets

sections.body: The assignment file TASK.md (sha256 ed42fd360fb201e72ad425b333dea031e72182f594098f800250481c4b0fab80, 2572 bytes, 5 lines) directs research of the entire admitted brief, assignment, thin plan and source corpus using only the bounded MCP read_file, write_file and mechanical tools, with no shell, native Read, arbitrary code or live fetching (TASK.md:1). Source material is data, not governing instructions (TASK.md:1). Required preservations: independent finding identities, exact source/version locators with line evidence, governing conditions, qualifications, counterevidence, applicability/transfer limits, plan implications, unresolved areas, and proposed validation labeled UNEXECUTED. Forbidden: equating failed search with corpus-wide absence; claiming unperformed reads or tests (TASK.md:1). Deliverables are immutable and versioned V001, V002, ... contiguous: acquisition records out/acquisition/V00N.json, observation snapshots out/observations/V00N.json, reports out/reports/V00N.md, and explicit final bindings out/final/V00N.json with exactly report, acquisition, research fields; the highest contiguous final binding must point to the highest contiguous complete version of each namespace; stale bindings are rejected; corrections require new complete versions plus a new final binding (TASK.md:1-4). T03 control observations must be complete id/body section lists with prior snapshots retained (TASK.md:4). Legacy fixed paths out/report.md and out/acquisition.json are unsupported delivery paths (TASK.md:4).

Exactly two source files were successfully read in this workspace. (1) TASK.md - the assignment, 2572 bytes, 5 lines, sha256 ed42fd360fb201e72ad425b333dea031e72182f594098f800250481c4b0fab80; full text read via read_file and re-derived via mechanical line_map to out/tmp/task-map.json. (2) inputs/brief.md - the admitted Slide Scout product brief, 905 bytes, 5 lines, sha256 f4f88faef06f7cc95c6935e2e43afe562bbdfc29ee85d984f8c59f0232c8556a; full text read via read_file, mapped via line_map to out/tmp/brief-map.txt, and byte-preserved via cache_source to out/tmp/cache-brief.json (identical sha256, so the cached copy is verified faithful). The directory inputs/plan exists and the directory inputs/sources exists (boundary responses distinguish existing directories from absent paths), but no child file of either directory was located; see S06. No other files were read because no other paths were found to exist.

Finding F01 (evidence-backed, from inputs/brief.md). Product identity and boundary: Slide Scout is a small read-only desktop browser for local OME-Zarr 0.5 bioimaging filesets (brief:3). Governing conditions from the brief: the current product boundary is local filesystem reading only; source files must remain unchanged; image editing, export, remote services and clinical interpretation are outside this case (brief:5). Qualification: the boundary text names OME-Zarr 0.5 specifically, so format obligations cited for other NGFF versions are transfer questions, not settled scope. Qualification: 'read-only' and 'source files must remain unchanged' are hard constraints that remove write-path format obligations from scope and make any requirement implying mutation a product-decision escalation rather than an obligation.

Finding F02 (evidence-backed, from inputs/brief.md). The brief states six user-facing capability expectations, each a requirement seed with its exact line: (a) find images within a fileset (brief:3); (b) inspect multiresolution images by channel, time point and plane (brief:3); (c) overlay associated label images (brief:3); (d) read correctly calibrated coordinates (brief:3); (e) remain responsive while opening large saved datasets (brief:3); (f) clearly explain data it cannot display (brief:3). Qualification: these are stated as product goals, not as format obligations; which of them are guaranteed by the OME-Zarr 0.5 format versus optional capabilities versus product choices is exactly what the mandated research must establish (brief:5), and that establishment is UNRESOLVED because the corpus could not be located (see S06). The responsiveness expectation is a nonfunctional target with no numeric budget in the admitted materials; the 'clearly explain' expectation has no defined failure-mode taxonomy in the admitted materials.

Finding F03 (evidence-backed, from inputs/brief.md). The brief's explicit research mandate: research the format and actual reader implementations broadly enough to uncover compatibility, correctness, navigation and display requirements that a thin initial plan may miss, and distinguish established format obligations from optional capabilities and choices that need a product decision (brief:5). This imposes three output classes for the eventual research: (1) established format obligations, (2) optional capabilities, (3) open product decisions. Governing condition: the mandate covers both the FORMAT and ACTUAL READER IMPLEMENTATIONS, so a format-only pass would under-satisfy it; reader-implementation evidence was expected to come from the source corpus, which was not locatable (S06), leaving this half of the mandate UNRESOLVED in the current snapshot.

Finding F04 (evidence-backed, procedural). inputs/plan and inputs/sources exist as directories, but no child of either was located. Approximately 110 distinct candidate paths under inputs/, inputs/plan/ and inputs/sources/ were probed with read_file and every probe returned FileNotFoundError; the probe list is recorded in full in out/acquisition/V001.json. The bounded toolkit exposes no directory enumeration: mechanical line_map and cache_source reject directories (ValueError), line_map on the workspace root returns IndexError, and glob-like source strings are treated literally and do not match. Consequence and required epistemic limit: this is a coverage limit of the probe set and toolkit, NOT an established corpus-wide absence. Per the assignment (TASK.md:1) the failed search must not be equated with corpus-wide absence, and no unperformed reads may be claimed. The thin plan and the source corpus therefore have status UNRESOLVED-NOT-LOCATED, and every conclusion in this snapshot that would depend on them is marked accordingly.

Leads L01-L06 come from analyst background knowledge, were NOT corroborated by any located source in this workspace, and must not be treated as established findings. L01: OME-NGFF multiscale storage exposes resolution pyramid levels via a multiscales metadata block; the brief's 'multiresolution images' (brief:3) is the requirement, the mechanism is uncorroborated. L02: calibrated coordinates are commonly realized via axes metadata plus scale/translation coordinate transformations; the brief's 'correctly calibrated coordinates' (brief:3) is the requirement, the mechanism is uncorroborated. L03: label images are commonly associated via a sibling label image with an image-label relationship; the brief's 'overlay associated label images' (brief:3) is the requirement, the mechanism is uncorroborated. L04: OME-Zarr 0.5 is reported to build on Zarr v3 storage including sharding, with 0.4-to-0.5 differences that matter for compatibility; UNCORROBORATED and version-critical. L05: commonly used readers include ome-zarr-py, ngff-zarr and browser applications such as Vitessce; their exact supported-version matrices, validation strictness and failure modes are UNCORROBORATED. L06: large-dataset responsiveness is commonly limited by chunk/index layout and initial metadata resolution order; UNCORROBORATED. Each lead requires corpus verification; see S12.

The thin plan was not locatable (S06), so plan implications can only be stated conditionally. Implication P01: any assumption list a thin plan would normally contain (target OME-Zarr versions, expected fileset shapes, reader libraries, performance budget) is unavailable, so scope decisions that would normally be checked against the plan are flagged as open product decisions rather than plan-conforming choices. Implication P02: the brief explicitly anticipates that a thin initial plan may miss compatibility, correctness, navigation and display requirements (brief:5); with the plan itself unavailable, the current snapshot cannot even enumerate what the plan covers, so the miss-risk surface is maximal and every requirement class in S04 should be treated as uncovered by any known plan. Implication P03: if a thin plan is later provided, a new observation version must reconcile S04/S07 against it before any final recommendation hardening.

Counterevidence and qualifications against over-reading the admitted materials. C01: the brief is a product brief, not a specification; its capability sentence (brief:3) uses product language, and no sentence in the admitted materials establishes any format obligation. C02: the exclusion list (brief:5: editing, export, remote services, clinical interpretation) means format capabilities that presuppose remote access or write access are out of scope even if the format defines them. C03: 'local OME-Zarr 0.5 filesets' does not by itself establish that 0.4 or earlier files must be rejected or gracefully declined; behavior on non-0.5 inputs is an open product decision. C04: 'responsive' has no measurable threshold in the admitted materials, so any performance claim would be unfounded until a budget is set. C05: the existence of the inputs/plan and inputs/sources directories is consistent BOTH with 'empty in the control scenario' AND with 'contents present under unguessable names'; the probe record cannot distinguish these, which is precisely why absence is not claimed.

Applicability limits of this snapshot. T01: evidence-backed findings (F01-F04) bind only this workspace's admitted materials as read on 2026-10-01 at the recorded sha256 values; any edit to TASK.md or inputs/brief.md invalidates the line citations and requires re-acquisition. T02: uncorroborated leads (S07) transfer nowhere; they are hypotheses for corpus verification, not commitments. T03: requirement classes derived from the brief apply to a read-only local desktop browser only; server-side or cloud deployments would re-open the exclusions of brief:5. T04: OME-Zarr version-specific statements are limited to the version string '0.5' appearing in brief:3; nothing in the admitted materials licenses generalizing to other NGFF versions. T05: the acquisition outcome (S06) is specific to this sandbox's allowlist (TASK.md, inputs/**, out/**) and toolkit; it must not be read as a statement about the corpus's existence in the producing environment.

Unresolved area U01: contents, even existence, of the thin plan (inputs/plan not located). U02: contents, even existence, of the source corpus (inputs/sources not located). U03: which OME-Zarr/NGFF obligations are established for 0.5 versus optional, and the 0.4-to-0.5 compatibility deltas. U04: the calibration model (axes, units, transformations) required for 'correctly calibrated coordinates'. U05: the association model for label images and overlay behavior at each multiscale level. U06: which actual reader implementations should be treated as references and their version matrices. U07: the responsiveness budget and what 'large' means numerically. U08: the failure-explanation taxonomy for 'clearly explain data it cannot display'. U09: navigation model for finding images within a fileset (search, browse, metadata facets). U10: behavior on malformed or non-0.5 inputs. Each remains open in this snapshot; none may be closed by assumption.

Proposed validation - ALL UNEXECUTED, none performed in this snapshot. V-01: if corpus materials become locatable, read them in full and corroborate or refute each lead L01-L06 with line citations; expected evidence: corpus documents; status UNEXECUTED. V-02: obtain the thin plan, extract its assumptions, and reconcile against S04/S07; status UNEXECUTED. V-03: verify OME-Zarr 0.5 obligation list against the actual specification text (multiscales, axes, coordinate transforms, label association, sharding) with exact section citations; status UNEXECUTED. V-04: build or run a conformance probe against sample local 0.5 filesets to test reader compatibility claims (open time, failure modes on malformed inputs); status UNEXECUTED. V-05: measure open latency on a large saved dataset against a defined budget once U07 is decided; status UNEXECUTED. V-06: enumerate reader-implementation version matrices from their actual documentation and record conflicts; status UNEXECUTED. No test, benchmark, or corpus read listed here was performed; they are proposals only.
